enrichment.summary: This executive order directs federal agencies to make it easier for Americans to hunt and access public lands by reducing restrictions and expanding hunting opportunities on federal lands. It also supports programs to encourage hunting among youth and veterans, promotes wildlife conservation efforts, and facilitates the donation of wild game meat to food assistance programs.
potential_concerns: Expanding hunting access and reducing restrictions on federal lands may adversely impact Environmental Justice Communities by increasing environmental degradation and diminishing equitable access to natural resources.
Encouraging hunting among youth and veterans could raise safety and ethical concerns if hunter education programs are inconsistently implemented, potentially harming youth participants.
Prioritizing hunting access and Sunday hunting expansions in rural communities could create conflicts with non-hunting residents and other recreational users.

Increased hunting to manage wildlife populations, including predator control, may disrupt ecosystems and face opposition from conservationists and Indigenous or tribal communities not explicitly mentioned.
Facilitating wild game meat donations may improve food assistance but also raises food safety and logistical challenges for food-insecure populations and assistance programs.
